solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criticise faulty camera in airline

parts.note: to pan a film or play is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: something faulty is not working properly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint about a broken camera found on board a passenger flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges CAMERA and IN together to give AMERICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan American World Airways, usually called Pan Am, was a major US carrier for decades.

clue.text: Languish in a posh 14

indicators.note: the verb goes inside the letters around it

parts.note: U means upper class, hence posh
to languish is to waste away, figuratively to die

explanation.surface: Wasting away in a smart setting while saying goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is FAREWELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, literally 'to God', used in English too.

clue.text: Unusually large island area in country

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so the letters of large are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surprisingly big island region within a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African nation, the largest on the continent by area.

clue.text: Without settling score I drive away

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: settling suggests things shifting into a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who leaves without paying a bill and simply drives off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settling' rearranges SCORE and I into ORCISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exorcise is to expel an evil spirit, driving it away.

clue.text: NEC quits mounted 11 for 14

indicators.note: mounted means going up, which in a down entry reads the letters backwards
quits means leaves, so these letters drop out of the other word

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, meaning wide as the sea
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trade-show venue checks out with a goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 less N, E, C leaves OAIC; 'mounted' turns it upward. 14 is FAREWELL. NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is an informal Italian goodbye, also used in English.

clue.text: Description of band as bad?

parts.note: bad is band with its N gone; N stands for name, so the word has lost its name

explanation.surface: A critic dismissing a pop group as terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a standard abbreviation for name; taking it out of band leaves bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a name is the sense: the word bad is band minus name, an anonymous version of it.

clue.text: Country initiating senior cinematic award for Ms Annis

parts.note: France is a European country

indicators.note: initiating means starting, so the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A nation launching a top film prize for an actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Francesca Annis is a British actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Her first name: Francesca Annis starred in Lillie and many TV and stage roles.

clue.text: Being stoned, hunk lacked inner energy. What an idiot!

indicators.note: the energy letter is placed inner, within the shuffled letters
being stoned means intoxicated, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A stoned hunk who has lost his drive looks a complete fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being stoned' rearranges HUNK LACKED; 'inner' sets E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A knucklehead is an informal term for a stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Biblical priest with power as a form of protection

indicators.note: the priest's name is taken with power in place of one of its letters, so one letter is swapped out

parts.note: Aaron, brother of Moses, was the first high priest of Israel
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: An Old Testament priest wears something powerful to keep himself safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' here means one A of AARON gives way to P.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is worn over clothes to shield them from dirt and spills, a simple form of protection.

clue.text: Reptile family's finally flourishing with firm support

parts.note: kin are one's family or relatives

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A snake whose family thrives, backed by a solid company.
explanation.definitionFit: The king cobra is the world's longest venomous snake, a reptile of South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Canoe adrift encounters a lot of ice wide as the sea

indicators.note: a canoe adrift has drifted out of its place, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a lot of the word, but not all of it: its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A drifting canoe meets a great expanse of ice in the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of ice' is ICE without its last letter, IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanic means belonging to or as vast as the ocean, so it fits something wide as the sea.

clue.text: Old carriage makes erratic circle around the outskirts of Uttoxeter

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the next piece, which sits inside them
erratic means irregular or unpredictable, so the letters of circle are jumbled
the outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of the town are taken

explanation.surface: An antique coach drives a wobbly loop round the edge of a Staffordshire market town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratic' turns CIRCLE into CRICLE; UR, the ends of Uttoxeter (a town in Staffordshire, England), goes in after the first C.
explanation.definitionFit: A curricle was a light two-wheeled carriage drawn by two horses, popular in Regency times.

clue.text: Provide support for type of 19D

parts.note: to cater is to provide food or what is needed
a pillar is a column that holds up a structure

explanation.surface: Supplying backing for a particular kind of lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 19D is VEHICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracked tractor or bulldozer is called a caterpillar, from its endless-track drive.

clue.text: Struggles with fellow in tangled forest

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in the jumbled letters
tangled means twisted together, so the letters of forest are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man fights his way through a dense, overgrown wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Efforts and struggles are both strenuous attempts to achieve something.

clue.text: See you! In autumn we're moving

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, so the shuffled letters sit within the season

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: moving means shifting about, so the letters of we're are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parting word to a friend who is relocating in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns WERE into REWE, which 'In' places inside FALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are things said when parting: 'see you!' is a casual goodbye.

clue.text: Deposit losing all rights of 14

indicators.note: losing all means every instance of the following letter is taken out

parts.note: tartar is the hard deposit that forms on teeth
R is the abbreviation for right, and the plural asks for each one

explanation.surface: A goodbye from someone whose deposit has been forfeited with all their rights.
explanation.walkthrough: TARTAR has two Rs; 'losing all rights' removes both. 14 is FAREWELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Elevated RC service location is hush-hush

indicators.note: elevated means raised up, which in a down entry reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: terce is the Roman Catholic office said at the third hour of the day
a spot is a place or location

explanation.surface: Where a raised Catholic ceremony takes place is kept confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' reverses TERCE plus SPOT, as fits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean highly confidential, kept strictly secret.

clue.text: Encourages transfers to another post

definitions.meaning: to second a proposal is to support it, encouraging its adoption
to second a worker is to move them temporarily to another job

explanation.surface: A manager who backs staff by moving them into new roles.
explanation.walkthrough: In the transfer sense the stress falls on the second syllable (se-CONDS), a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verb senses: backing a motion, and temporarily reassigning an employee elsewhere.

clue.text: 14 for example's willing to join Australian gunners

parts.note: say means for example, as in 'take, say, ten'
on means willing, as in 'are you on?'
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British army

explanation.surface: A volunteer joins an Australian artillery unit with a goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is FAREWELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sayonara is the Japanese word for goodbye.

clue.text: Trembling I faced new, ultimately supreme challenge

indicators.note: trembling means shaking, so these letters are shaken into a new order
ultimately points to the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A nervous person facing a fresh, top-level test.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance, a challenge to authority.

clue.text: French article follows state in 14

indicators.note: follows means the article comes after the state

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A French word follows the name of a state in a goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is FAREWELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Vale is Latin for 'be well', used in English as a solemn goodbye.

clue.text: See what I regularly called HGV perhaps

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see
eh? is a way of saying what?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: Someone pointing out what they named their heavy goods lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: HGV is a heavy goods vehicle, the British term for a large lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: An HGV is one example of a motorised transport, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Catastrophic pay cuts involve hardships essentially for weak fellow

indicators.note: the shuffled letters involve, or enclose, the next piece
catastrophic suggests something wrecked, so the letters of pay cuts are rearranged
essentially points to the essence, the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Disastrous wage cuts bring hardship, a complaint about a feeble man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catastrophic' rearranges PAY CUTS; the central letter of hardships, S, goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pussycat is informal for a soft, gentle or easily handled man, a weakling.

clue.text: Special male adult's taken in by helpful member of gang maybe

indicators.note: these letters are taken in by the next word, which surrounds them

parts.note: kind means helpful and considerate
he is the male pronoun
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A man taken in by a kindly person who helps out a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: A skinhead is a youth with a shaven head, part of a British subculture often seen in gangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinheads often ran in groups, so a gang member is a plausible example, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Type of 19D could become very cold with the addition of carbon

indicators.note: the answer would become the cold word if a letter were added, so that letter is missing from it

parts.note: arctic means extremely cold
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A lorry that might freeze over if it took on carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: adding C to the answer would give the cold word. 19D is VEHICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a large truck with a separate cab.

clue.text: Insects covering enclosure leave

indicators.note: the insects cover, or surround, the next piece

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosure, as on a letter

explanation.surface: Bugs swarming over a pen or a document enclosed with a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave in the sense of permission: a licence grants permission to do something.

clue.text: Middle of 14 overturned vessel

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, which in a down entry reads the letters from the bottom
middle of means the outer two letters at each end are dropped

parts.note: the answer to 14 across, a parting word

explanation.surface: A dish knocked over during a parting.
explanation.walkthrough: The central four letters of 14 are REWE, which 'overturned' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug, a vessel for water.

clue.text: With cold, old stains spoiled panels

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Damp and age have marked a room's wood with stains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges C, O and STAINS into AINSCOTS after W.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscots are wooden panels lining the lower part of interior walls.

clue.text: Muslim prince is consistently warm to English queen

indicators.note: consistently suggests a steady pattern, so alternate letters of the word are taken

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A Muslim ruler shows steady warmth towards an English monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of warm give AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ameer is a variant spelling of emir, a Muslim ruler or prince.

clue.text: In a rage American driver abandoned man in 14

indicators.note: being in a rage means wild with anger, so the letters are thrown into disorder
abandoned says the three letters of the word that follows are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: An angry American motorist leaves someone behind with a goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: AMERICAN DRIVER less the letters of MAN leaves ERICADRIVER, which 'In a rage' rearranges. 14 is FAREWELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrivederci is Italian for goodbye, literally 'until we see each other again'.
